findings.title: Login-cache invalidation on update evaluates the stored IDP through the org-aware wrapper, so updates to IDPs in a disabled org skip invalidation
findings.body: In update(), `idpById` comes from getById(), which wraps the model in createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel. That wrapper's isEnabled() returns false whenever the bound organization is disabled, while `model` (the updated raw representation) reports the IDP's own enabled flag. For an IDP bound to a disabled org, getLoginPredicate().test(original) is therefore always false. The login lists are built from the JPA query, which does not consider org state, so such an IDP can be cached. If the update then disables it (or hides it / makes it link-only), both sides evaluate to false, registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate returns early, and the cached login list keeps the now-disabled IDP. A later getForLogin cache hit returns it; the uncached path would exclude it. The stale entry persists after the org is re-enabled. Callers that do not re-check isEnabled() will expose a disabled IDP. The login decision should use the raw stored model (e.g. idpDelegate.getById), not the org-aware wrapper.

findings.title: Cleanup never removes the created IDPs (get("alias")::remove), leaking 21 IDPs into the shared test realm
findings.body: `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove)` binds the method reference to a resource for the literal alias "alias", which does not exist. Each registered cleanup therefore targets a nonexistent IDP, and the idp-alias-0..20 providers created by this test are never deleted. The same bug exists at line 425 for idp-alias-20 and at line 303 in testCacheIDPByOrg, which this test copies. The leftover IDPs (several of them enabled, public, and linked to an organization) remain in the realm for later tests. Any test that asserts exact login or organization IDP counts can then fail depending on test execution order. The cleanup should reference each created alias.

findings.title: getForLogin javadoc omits the new organization BROKER_PUBLIC requirement
findings.body: The javadoc says an IDP can be used for login if it is enabled, not link-only, and not hidden on login. The getLoginPredicate() change in this PR adds a further rule: an IDP bound to an organization must also have BROKER_PUBLIC=true to qualify. The public contract documented here is now incomplete, and callers of getForLogin cannot learn the rule from the interface.

findings.title: REALM_ONLY lookups get separate cache entries per organizationId even though the organization is ignored
findings.body: searchKey is derived from organizationId for every mode. For FetchMode.REALM_ONLY the delegate ignores organizationId, so getForLogin(REALM_ONLY, orgA) and getForLogin(REALM_ONLY, null) produce identical results but are stored under different searchKeys in the same IdentityProviderListQuery. The same realm-only list is duplicated per distinct organization id that is passed in. Normalising searchKey to "" for REALM_ONLY would avoid the duplicate entries.

findings.title: No test covers the invalidation cases the new BROKER_PUBLIC predicate and org disable handling exist for
findings.body: The new `idp.getOrganizationId() == null || BROKER_PUBLIC` clause in getLoginPredicate() is only exercised indirectly. Step 4 links a realm-level login IDP to an organization, but nothing checks that flipping BROKER_PUBLIC from true to false on an organization-bound login IDP invalidates the login caches. Nothing covers an IDP bound to a disabled organization either, which is the case where the stored-state evaluation in update() goes wrong. Regressions in either path would leave stale login lists undetected.
